Preprint — arXiv:2609.00252v1 [cs.SE]; footer 'Manuscript submitted to ACM' (venue not named)
Universidad Politécnica de Madrid, Spain (all four authors)

Conceptual; secondary: Review — socio-technical model of SDD, harness characterisation with worked examples, typology of five interaction patterns; built on a multivocal literature review (four databases and grey literature, IC/EC stated)
fields.why: Still open. Section 3 (pp. 8-10) names its sources (IEEE Xplore, ACM DL, Scopus, arXiv, grey-literature domains) and IC/EC (Table 3), so under the 2026-11-23 rule the review part 'describes its search' and could be assessed with DARE. But contributions C1-C3 (p. 4) are a model, a harness and a typology, the abstract calls the method a 'conceptual analysis', and the paper presents its own eight-mechanism methodological harness (p. 14: 'our contribution is their organization into a coherent methodological harness'), so 'Proposes an approach' is also defensible as main nature. Author decides; this decides Q1-Q13 vs DARE (Q13 applies under Conceptual or Proposes an approach).

fields.v: SDD as a team-level discipline for Agentic Software Engineering with a 'methodological harness' of eight mechanisms (authors' framework), no version, no tool. Tools mentioned as examples only: Claude Code, OpenCode, Codex (technical harness), OpenSpec-style proposal-apply-archive cycle

System specifications (architecture, conventions, domain models, normative rules) materialised as always-loaded rule files (agent.md, CLAUDE.md, .cursorrules, AGENTS.md); feature specifications per change (intent, acceptance criteria in Given-When-Then, constraints, decisions), archived when delivered; skills (SKILL.md, loaded on demand); persistent shared knowledge store (decisions, rationale, session summaries); consultation records; evidence packs (acceptance tests mapped to clauses, CI output, rationale, links to spec and rules); workflow definitions with autonomy levels

Iterative cycle over specifications: proposal (lightweight spec enriched iteratively) -> apply (agent derives artefacts, suspends to consult on ambiguity) -> archive (verified spec committed; later changes reference it). Harness mechanisms: H1 context engineering, H2 persistent shared knowledge, H3 executable specifications, H4 N-version parallel agents (git worktrees), H5 normative specifications, H6 structured consultation, H7 evidence-backed acceptance, H8 graduated autonomy

Briefing (human writes/approves spec, with review of briefs); structured consultation when agent suspends on ambiguity; review of evidence packs against the spec before acceptance; norm encoding via reviewed PR; autonomy calibrated per task class (e.g. auth changes need human-approved plan and step-wise review; dependency patches fully autonomous)
Not run, document-based (worked examples are the authors' fictitious constructions)

Not classified in Böckeler terms; authors' wording: specification is the 'source of truth', version-controlled with code, artefacts derived with provenance, disagreements resolved by re-deriving the artefact or amending the spec, 'never by silent edits' (closest to spec-anchored); feature specs archived after delivery, system specs (rule files) kept and maintained
fields.why: Authors do not use Böckeler's terms. Specification as 'source of truth', version-controlled with the code, disagreements resolved by re-deriving the artefact or amending the spec, 'never by silent edits' (p. 11) fits spec-anchored; derivation of all artefacts from the spec could be read as spec-as-source; feature specs 'archived once delivered' (p. 11) point to spec-first at feature level, while system specs (rule files) are maintained.

Framework not empirically validated; benefits are predictions; terms unstable; operational details will date quickly; evidence skews to web/SaaS/platform engineering, regulated and embedded domains unanalysed; no adoption or maturity model proposed. Risks: talent bifurcation, cultural fracture, cost spiral, specification drift, platform lock-in; SDD may be premature for exploratory work. Research agenda RA1-RA5: team dynamics, validation of interaction patterns, orchestration competences, adoption pathways, measurement frameworks
